l4_steps.name: Ingest competitor fare data via ATPCO feed
l4_steps.input: Daily ATPCO Type A/B/C fare change transactions
l4_steps.output: Competitor fare matrix by O&D pair and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: Feed ingestion latency ≤15 min from ATPCO publication window
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare filings lag real-time competitor NDC-direct pricing by 20-40 min, creating competitive blind spots on 20-30% of market fares during high-demand windows

l4_steps.name: Load demand signals and booking pace from NRM
l4_steps.input: Booking curve data, load factor forecasts, O&D demand segmentation
l4_steps.output: Demand signal dataset per flight-date-cabin combination
l4_steps.kpi: Demand signal refresh cycle ≤4 hrs for departures within 0–14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM demand forecasts calibrated on historical booking patterns underweight demand spikes from social media trends or flash sales by competitors, skewing price recommendations

l4_steps.name: Validate data completeness and quality gate
l4_steps.input: Competitor fare matrix and NRM demand signal dataset
l4_steps.output: Data quality scorecard; ingestion batch approved or rejected
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness score ≥95% before optimization run proceeds
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing competitor fare data on thin routes (sub-daily frequency) triggers default pricing rules that undercut yield targets by 10–15% on marginal markets

l4_steps.name: Configure fare class elasticity parameters
l4_steps.input: Historical booking data, price-response curves, market segment definitions
l4_steps.output: Elasticity parameter set by market, segment, and season
l4_steps.kpi: Parameter review cycle ≤30 days; elasticity model R² ≥0.85 per market cluster
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM elasticity models require minimum 12 months of booking history — new or thin routes lack sufficient data for reliable calibration, requiring manual overrides that degrade model integrity

l4_steps.name: Set fare floor and ceiling guardrail rules
l4_steps.input: Approved tariff schedule, cost floor benchmarks, revenue targets
l4_steps.output: Min/max fare bounds per booking class and market pair
l4_steps.kpi: Guardrail coverage 100% of active markets before each daily optimization run
l4_steps.pain_point: Cost floor benchmarks require coordinated input from Finance (SAP S/4HANA FI/CO) but finance data latency averages 24–48 hrs, creating risk of stale floor values during fuel price volatility

l4_steps.name: Review and approve pricing model configuration
l4_steps.input: Elasticity parameter set and guardrail rule configuration
l4_steps.output: Approved pricing model configuration; version-tagged snapshot in audit log
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration approval cycle ≤4 hrs for routine updates; ≤24 hrs for structural changes
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM configuration lacks automated rollback capability — a misconfigured elasticity parameter can propagate to thousands of published fares before detection, requiring manual ATPCO correction filings

l4_steps.name: Run dynamic pricing optimization engine
l4_steps.input: Approved model configuration, demand signals, competitor fare matrix
l4_steps.output: Optimized fare recommendation set per flight-date-cabin
l4_steps.kpi: Optimization run completion ≤20 min for full network; recommendation coverage ≥98% of active O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM compute time exceeds SLA during IROPS events when demand signals are highly volatile, delaying fare updates during the highest-yield recovery window by 30–60 min

l4_steps.name: Apply business rules overlay and sanity checks
l4_steps.input: Raw optimization output from pricing engine
l4_steps.output: Rule-adjusted fare set with full audit log of modifications
l4_steps.kpi: Business rule violation rate ≤0.5% of recommended fares per optimization run
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated ceiling rules set for normal demand periods suppress legitimately high fares during demand surges, capping revenue on peak routes by an estimated 3–5% during holiday windows

l4_steps.name: Validate fare recommendations against guardrails
l4_steps.input: Rule-adjusted fare set from business rules overlay
l4_steps.output: Validated fare set approved for filing; exception list flagged for manual review
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-approval rate ≥90% of recommendations; manual review queue cleared within 30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing windows (20-min cycles) create time pressure that incentivises skipping manual review of exception fares, increasing risk of erroneous public fares reaching GDS and NDC channels

l4_steps.name: File approved fare set to ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Validated fare set with booking classes, rules, and effective dates
l4_steps.output: ATPCO fare transaction records; filed fare effective timestamps
l4_steps.kpi: Filing-to-live latency ≤20 min (ATPCO standard distribution cycle)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing errors (invalid rule codes, tariff mismatches) trigger rejection queues requiring manual re-filing, delaying competitive fare responses by 40–60 min during time-sensitive price match windows

l4_steps.name: Distribute fares across GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Amadeus GDS / Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS
l4_steps.input: Filed ATPCO fares and NDC dynamic offer parameters
l4_steps.output: Published fares active across all indirect and direct distribution channels
l4_steps.kpi: GDS channel sync latency ≤30 min; NDC direct channel sync ≤5 min post-filing
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fare synchronisation lags behind NDC direct channels by 20–25 min, creating temporary price disparities that trigger OTA parity violation claims under distribution agreements

l4_steps.name: Confirm fare availability in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Distribution confirmation messages from GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.output: Fare availability audit report; PSS-confirmed live status
l4_steps.kpi: PSS availability confirmation within 35 min of ATPCO filing; availability accuracy ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa availability caching can serve stale fares to agents for up to 15 min after updates, causing booking conflicts and involuntary re-pricing that generates customer service escalations

l4_steps.name: Monitor live fare performance and revenue metrics
l4_steps.input: Booking transactions, yield actuals, load factor by flight-date
l4_steps.output: Real-time pricing performance dashboard; automated alert triggers
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue variance vs. forecast ≤±5%; alert response time ≤15 min from threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS Redshift analytics pipeline has 5–10 min data latency, insufficient to detect and correct pricing errors on high-frequency short-haul routes before significant booking volume accumulates at wrong fares

l4_steps.name: Detect pricing anomaly and trigger override review
l4_steps.input: Performance dashboard alerts and deviation threshold breaches
l4_steps.output: Override recommendation; escalation decision to Pricing Manager
l4_steps.kpi: Anomaly-to-action cycle ≤30 min; false positive alert rate ≤10%
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM anomaly detection thresholds tuned for normal operations generate excessive false positives during promotional events, causing alert fatigue and delayed response to genuine pricing errors

l4_steps.name: Apply manual fare override and document rationale
l4_steps.input: Approved override decision with business justification
l4_steps.output: Override fare filed to ATPCO; audit trail record; model feedback flag
l4_steps.kpi: Override filing completion ≤20 min; override documentation rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual overrides not fed back as PROS RM training signals cause the engine to repeatedly recommend the same suboptimal fares, creating a costly correction loop that accounts for 15–20% of analyst override volume

l4_steps.name: Assess model performance and revenue uplift
l4_steps.input: Monthly revenue actuals vs. RM optimization recommendations
l4_steps.output: Model performance scorecard; recalibration flag with supporting analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Dynamic pricing revenue uplift ≥3% vs. static pricing baseline; model MAPE ≤8%
l4_steps.pain_point: Attributing revenue uplift to dynamic pricing vs. schedule changes, competitor capacity, or ancillary revenue requires controlled experiment design that lacks standardised methodology at most carriers

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate model and release updated configuration
l4_steps.output: Updated model configuration; version-tagged release with change log
l4_steps.kpi: Recalibration cycle ≤30 days; post-recalibration uplift improvement ≥1% within 14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM model recalibration requires a 2–4 week data stabilisation period post-change, during which the system operates with lower confidence scores, increasing override frequency and analyst workload by 25–30%
